components.name: 3U CubeSat
components.description: Loaf-of-bread sized. Cheap and light, fits 1 instrument.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (typical CubeSat ranges): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: 6U CubeSat
components.description: Shoebox sized. Fits 2 instruments.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (typical CubeSat ranges): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: 12U CubeSat
components.description: Small-suitcase sized. Fits 3 instruments.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (typical CubeSat ranges): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: ESPA-class SmallSat
components.description: Mini-fridge sized. Heavy and pricey, but tough and long-lived.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (small satellite ranges): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: Body-mounted cells
components.description: Solar cells glued to the sides. Light, but little power.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Power chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
components.note: Estimate: power in full sunlight near Earth.

components.name: Small deployable wings
components.description: Panels that unfold after launch, like wings.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Power chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
components.note: Estimate: power in full sunlight near Earth.

components.name: Large deployable wings
components.description: Big unfolding wings for power-hungry missions.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Power chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
components.note: Estimate: power in full sunlight near Earth.

components.name: SmallSat solar array
components.description: Large rigid array. Lots of power, lots of mass.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Power chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
components.note: Estimate: power in full sunlight near Earth.

components.name: 40 Wh battery
components.description: Phone-power-bank class. Fine for tiny spacecraft.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Power chapter, lithium-ion batteries): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: 100 Wh battery
components.description: Laptop-battery class.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Power chapter, lithium-ion batteries): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: 300 Wh battery
components.description: Big pack for long shadows or hungry instruments.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Power chapter, lithium-ion batteries): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: 1 kWh battery
components.description: SmallSat-class battery. Heavy but lasts many cycles.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Power chapter, lithium-ion batteries): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: UHF radio
components.description: Simple, cheap radio. Very slow: like texting your data home.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Communications chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
components.note: Estimate: daily volume from low Earth orbit with a few ground passes.

components.name: S-band radio
components.description: Medium-speed radio used by many small missions.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Communications chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
components.note: Estimate: daily volume from low Earth orbit with a few ground passes.

components.name: X-band radio
components.description: Fast radio for data-heavy imaging missions. Needs more power.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Communications chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
components.note: Estimate: daily volume from low Earth orbit with a few ground passes.

components.name: Deep-space transponder + dish
components.description: Radio plus high-gain antenna built to talk to Earth from far away.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Communications chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
components.note: Estimate: rated as if in low Earth orbit; distance shrinks it a lot.

components.name: Basic computer
components.description: Simple flight computer with small storage.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Command & Data Handling chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: Standard computer
components.description: Reliable computer with more storage.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Command & Data Handling chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: Onboard-processing computer
components.description: Processes images in orbit and only sends what matters: halves your data.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Command & Data Handling chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
components.note: Estimate: 50% data reduction is a gameplay simplification.

components.name: Radiation-hardened computer
components.description: Built to survive radiation for many years. Expensive.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Command & Data Handling chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: Magnetorquers only
components.description: Uses Earth's magnetic field to turn. Rough pointing only.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Guidance, Navigation & Control chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
components.note: Estimate. Simplification: works everywhere in this game.

components.name: Reaction wheels
components.description: Spinning wheels that turn the spacecraft. Good pointing.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Guidance, Navigation & Control chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: Wheels + star tracker
components.description: A star camera tells you exactly where you point. Precise.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Guidance, Navigation & Control chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

components.name: SmallSat precision ADCS
components.description: Heavy-duty precise pointing system with long life.
components.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Guidance, Navigation & Control chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/

instruments.name: Wide-field camera
instruments.description: Takes color pictures of large areas.
instruments.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Science Instruments chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
instruments.note: Estimate; science value is a game score.

instruments.name: Thermal infrared camera
instruments.description: Sees heat. Spots fires and hot spots, day or night.
instruments.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Science Instruments chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
instruments.note: Estimate; science value is a game score.

instruments.name: Hyperspectral imager
instruments.description: Splits light into hundreds of colors to identify materials. Lots of data.
instruments.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Science Instruments chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
instruments.note: Estimate; science value is a game score.

instruments.name: Ground-penetrating radar
instruments.description: Bounces radio waves to see below the surface, e.g. buried ice.
instruments.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Science Instruments chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
instruments.note: Estimate; science value is a game score.

instruments.name: Magnetometer
instruments.description: Measures magnetic fields, like a super-sensitive compass.
instruments.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Science Instruments chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
instruments.note: Estimate; science value is a game score.

instruments.name: Energetic particle detector
instruments.description: Counts fast particles blasted out by the Sun.
instruments.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Science Instruments chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
instruments.note: Estimate; science value is a game score.

instruments.name: Solar X-ray monitor
instruments.description: Watches the Sun for flares that cause space weather.
instruments.source: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology State-of-the-Art report (Science Instruments chapter): https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/
instruments.note: Estimate; science value is a game score.

orbits.name: Very Low Earth Orbit
orbits.description: Super close to Earth: sharpest pictures, but thin air drags you down within a year.
orbits.source: NASA Earth Observatory, Catalog of Earth Satellite Orbits: https://earthobservatory.nasa.gov/features/OrbitsCatalog
orbits.note: Estimate: lifetime and contact factors simplified for gameplay.

orbits.name: Sun-synchronous LEO
orbits.description: Classic Earth-watching orbit: passes over each place at the same local time every day.
orbits.source: NASA Earth Observatory, Catalog of Earth Satellite Orbits: https://earthobservatory.nasa.gov/features/OrbitsCatalog

orbits.name: Geostationary orbit
orbits.description: Hovers over one spot on Earth. Always in view of its ground station, but far away.
orbits.source: NASA Earth Observatory, Catalog of Earth Satellite Orbits: https://earthobservatory.nasa.gov/features/OrbitsCatalog
orbits.note: Estimate: contact factor combines always-in-view with long distance.

orbits.name: Sun–Earth L1 point
orbits.description: A balance point between Earth and Sun: a front-row seat to solar storms. Never in shadow.
orbits.source: NASA space weather missions at L1 (e.g. ACE, DSCOVR) public mission pages

orbits.name: Low Mars orbit
orbits.description: Orbiting Mars. Sunlight is weaker and Earth is very far, so data trickles home slowly.
orbits.source: NASA Mars Exploration public facts (sunlight at Mars ≈ 43% of Earth's): https://science.nasa.gov/mars/
orbits.note: Estimate: contact factor simplified for gameplay.

launchVehicles.name: Rideshare slot (LEO)
launchVehicles.description: Share a rocket with other satellites. Cheap, but strict size limit and no choice of far destinations.
launchVehicles.source: Estimate based on publicly listed rideshare prices; generic vehicle class, not a specific product.

launchVehicles.name: Deep-space secondary payload
launchVehicles.description: Ride along with a big mission heading far away. Small size limit.
launchVehicles.source: Estimate based on NASA secondary-payload opportunities on larger missions; generic class.

launchVehicles.name: Small dedicated launcher
launchVehicles.description: A whole small rocket just for you. Pick your exact orbit near Earth.
launchVehicles.source: Estimate based on publicly reported small-launcher prices; generic vehicle class, not a specific product.

launchVehicles.name: Medium-lift rocket
launchVehicles.description: A big rocket that can send heavy spacecraft almost anywhere. Very expensive.
launchVehicles.source: Estimate based on publicly reported medium-lift launch prices; generic vehicle class, not a specific product.

objectives.name: Earth Watcher
objectives.description: Firefighters need fresh images of wildfires every day. Build a small satellite that sees heat or images the land from low Earth orbit.
objectives.source: Scenario inspired by NASA Earth science wildfire monitoring; requirements are game values.

objectives.name: Storm Sentinel
objectives.description: Solar storms can knock out power grids and satellites. Station a monitor between Earth and the Sun to give early warning.
objectives.source: Scenario inspired by NASA space weather missions at L1; requirements are game values.

objectives.name: Red Planet Scout
objectives.description: Future explorers need maps of Mars. Send a small orbiter to image the surface or search for buried ice.
objectives.source: Scenario inspired by NASA Mars orbiter science; requirements are game values.

events.name: Solar flare
events.description: A burst of radiation forces heaters and safe mode on. Power use jumps 20% for a day.
events.source: Simplified scenario inspired by NASA space weather effects on spacecraft.

events.name: Ground station outage
events.description: A storm on Earth shuts the antenna for 3 days. Data must wait in onboard storage.

events.name: Launch delay
events.description: The rocket slips by months. Extra costs eat 10% of your launch price.

events.name: Micrometeoroid hit
events.description: A grain of dust damages a solar panel. You lose 8% of your power for good.

events.name: Battery cold snap
events.description: A heater glitch chills the battery. It holds 30% less energy.
